title: Towards Generalisable Video Moment Retrieval: Visual-Dynamic Injection to Image-Text Pre-Training

problems.name: Boundary Ambiguity and Localization Precision
problems.evidence_sentence: For the fine-grained retrieval objective of VMR, the precise segment-wise temporal boundary labels are intuitively harder to be collected than conventional image/video-level annotations.

problems.name: Domain Shift and Generalization
problems.evidence_sentence: Especially, VDI yields notable advantages when being tested on the out-of-distribution splits where the testing samples involve novel scenes and vocabulary. # Abstract The correlation between the vision and text is essential for video moment retrieval (VMR), however, existing methods heavily rely on separate pre-training feature extractors for visual and textual understanding.

problems.name: Cross-Modal Semantic Alignment Gap
problems.evidence_sentence: Without sufficient temporal boundary annotations, it is non-trivial to learn universal video-text alignments.

methods.name: Benchmark or Dataset Construction
methods.evidence_sentence: The VDI method is a generic formulation that can be integrated into existing VMR models and benefits them from the universal visual-textual alignments derived from large-scale imagetext data. (3) The VDI achieves the state-of-the-art performances on two standard VMR benchmark datasets.
